record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let a(n,m) be the probability that the harmonic descent chain started from n ever visits state m, and let a(m)=lim_{n→∞} a(n,m). Find explicit bounds on |a(n,m)-a(m)|. In particular, prove the stated Ansatz: for any nonnegative sequence f(j)=O(j^k), if Σ_{j≥2} a(j)f(j) converges then Σ_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j) converges to that sum, and if Σ_{j≥2} a(j)f(j) diverges then Σ_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j) is asymptotic to Σ_{j=2}^n a(j)f(j).

evidence.quote: a(n, i) := probability that the chain started at state n is ever in state i. (49)
Open Problem 8 Find explicit bounds for |a(n, m) − a(m)|. In particular, prove the following Ansatz.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Markov chain on the integers $\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ called the harmonic descent chain, defined as follows. For $n\ge 2$, let $h_{n-1}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}1/j$. From state $n\ge 2$, the chain jumps to state $i\in\{1,2,\ldots,n-1\}$ with probability
$$p(n,i)=\frac{1}{h_{n-1}}\cdot\frac{1}{n-i},\qquad 1\le i\le n-1,$$
and state $1$ is absorbing. For integers $n\ge m\ge 1$, define
$$a(n,m)=\Pr\big(\text{the chain started at } n \text{ ever visits state } m\big),$$
with the convention $a(n,n)=1$. It is known that the limit
$$a(m)=\lim_{n\to\infty} a(n,m)$$
exists for every $m\ge 1$.

(a) Find explicit (quantitative) bounds for $|a(n,m)-a(m)|$ as $n\to\infty$ with $m$ fixed (and, more generally, jointly in $n$ and $m$).

(b) Prove the following Ansatz. Let $f:\{2,3,\ldots\}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfy $f(j)=O(j^k)$ for some $k\ge 0$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] If $\sum_{j\ge 2} a(j)f(j)<\infty$, then 
$$\sum_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j)\ \longrightarrow\ \sum_{j\ge 2} a(j)f(j)\quad\text{as } n\to\infty.$$
\item[(ii)] If $\sum_{j\ge 2} a(j)f(j)=\infty$, then 
$$\sum_{j=2}^n a(n,j)f(j)\ \sim\ \sum_{j=2}^n a(j)f(j)\quad\text{as } n\to\infty.$$
\end{itemize}
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 follow-up work establishes explicit polynomial bounds of the form $c(k,\varepsilon)(n/k)^{-\gamma_*-\varepsilon}\le a(n,k)-a(k)\le C(k,\varepsilon)(n/k)^{-\gamma_*+\varepsilon}$ for an implicit exponent $\gamma_*\approx 1.567$, and proves the convergent case of the Ansatz for $f(k)=O(k^{-\varepsilon})$. The full Ansatz for general polynomial-growth $f(j)=O(j^k)$ (in particular the divergent-sum asymptotic equivalence) does not appear to be fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics for the harmonic descent chain and applications to critical beta-splitting trees
status_evidence.claim: Explicit two-sided polynomial bounds for a(n,k)-a(k) with exponent γ*≈1.567 are established.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics for the harmonic descent chain (HTML)
status_evidence.snippet: a similar analysis ... proves the following case of Ansatz 20: Σ_{k=2}^n a(n,k)f(k) → Σ_{k=2}^∞ a(k)f(k) for f(k)=O(k^{-ε})
status_evidence.claim: The convergent case of the Ansatz is proved under decay condition f(k)=O(k^{-ε}).

status_evidence.title: The Harmonic Descent Chain
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the harmonic descent chain underlying the critical beta-splitting tree.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work introducing and analyzing the chain a(n,m) and limit a(m).
